page: Amazon Web Services i7i.xlarge is a storage-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8559C processor operating at 3.2 GHz, configured with 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory running at 6 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, a 937 GB NVMe SSD is bundled directly with the instance. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results show strong single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2299.0 placing it in the top tier (top 10%). Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression (34.34 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (14.1 GB/sec) also rank in the top 25%. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics show some limitations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance (4390.87) and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression (28.17 GB/sec) are categorized as weak, as is the memory bandwidth for read-only small blocks (343.61 GB/sec) and large blocks (33.73 GB/sec). Passmark database operations (3276.07) and static web serving throughput (8.15 GB/sec) perform at average levels.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the i7i.xlarge offers a high density of local NVMe SSD storage and DDR5 memory relative to its 4 vCPU count, making it a specialized option for storage-heavy workloads without requiring excessive compute resources. The presence of advanced CPU instruction sets, such as Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512, supports specialized workloads like low-latency vector operations and cryptography. This instance is best suited for local database hosting, caching layers, and storage-intensive applications that benefit from high single-core performance and fast local NVMe storage, though it may be less optimal for highly parallelized multi-core compute tasks.
